reconcile.note: Gill argues Jehoiada and Barachias were two names for Zechariah's father, both meaning praise or bless the Lord, harmonizing Matthew with Chronicles.

discrepancy.note: Strauss presses the point directly: the Zechariah murdered in 2 Chronicles 24:20 was son of Jehoiada, not Barachiah, so Matthew has confused him with the prophet Zechariah.

quotes.text: the innocent blood shed from that of Abel to that of Zacharias, the son of Barachias, slain in the temple, will be required of their generation. The Zacharias of whom such an end is narrated 2 Chron. xxiv. 20 ff. was a son, not of Barachias, but of Jehoiada.
quotes.attr: David Friedrich Strauss (d. 1874), The Life of Jesus Critically Examined, trans. George Eliot (1846), on Matthew 23:35 and 2 Chronicles 24:20.

sides.snippet: Zechariah the son of Jehoiada the priest
sides.verseText: The Spirit of God came on Zechariah the son of Jehoiada the priest; and he stood above the people, and said to them, Thus says God, Why disobey you the commandments of Yahweh, so that you can't prosper? because you have forsaken Yahweh, he has also forsaken you.

sides.snippet: the blood of Zachariah son of Barachiah
sides.verseText: that on you may come all the righteous blood shed on the earth, from the blood of righteous Abel to the blood of Zachariah son of Barachiah, whom you killed between the sanctuary and the altar.
